description: REQ-G2 step (b) runtime verification has a hash-replay loophole that defeats the entire INV-13 active half (the very thing FIND-015 was promoted to required:true to fix). The spec states: 'The runner SHALL verify every event:"earn" row by re-issuing the platform API call referenced in platform_api_call.endpoint and checking that the response sha256 matches platform_api_response_sha256.' The match is only between (re-fetched response) and (skill-declared response_sha256). The runner NEVER checks that the receipt_id / amount_jpy / amount_usdc / payer values in the event row actually appear in the platform-API response body. A malicious or hallucinating skill can therefore: (1) pick any legitimate, idempotent endpoint the skill is allowed to call (e.g. `GET /v1/account/health`, `GET /v1/me`, an authenticated-but-trivial endpoint that returns deterministic data), (2) compute the real sha256 of that response, (3) emit `{event:"earn", receipt_id:"FAKE-123", amount_jpy: 100000, platform_api_call:{endpoint:"/v1/me", response_sha256: <real_hash>}}`, (4) runner re-fetches /v1/me, the response hashes to the same real_hash, runner appends the forged earnings row to earnings.jsonl, (5) cumulative_jpy_earned inflates, REQ-B4 kill-switch is defeated, ROI dashboard is poisoned, and TRAP-1 (reward hacking) is reactivated despite the spec claiming to close it. PROP-G2-runtime is required:true but only tests 'fake event with no matching response_sha256 is rejected' — it does not test 'forged receipt_id paired with real-but-benign endpoint sha256 is rejected' because the spec does not require that rejection. As-spec'd, INV-13 active half guarantees only 'the response the skill claimed to see is the response the API actually returned' — it does NOT guarantee 'the receipt the skill claims is in that response is actually in it'. The fix requires REQ-G2(b) to bind: (i) endpoint must be a settled-payout / receipt-lookup endpoint (allowlist per platform), AND (ii) runner must parse the re-fetched response and confirm receipt_id, amount_jpy, amount_usdc, payer all appear in the response body with matching values, AND (iii) PROP-G2-runtime fixture must include the 'plausible-endpoint + forged receipt' attack.

evidence.snippet: The runner SHALL verify every `event: "earn"` row by re-issuing the platform API call referenced in `platform_api_call.endpoint` and checking that the response sha256 matches `platform_api_response_sha256`. ONLY on match SHALL the runner append the corresponding row to `earnings.jsonl`
